image.alt: A peace lily in a white pot, with glossy dark leaves and white flowers

snap: An elegant indoor staple known for glossy dark leaves and striking white spathes that signal thirst by gently drooping before springing back after watering.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to tropical rainforests of Central and South America; forms dense clumps of dark green foliage up to 1–3 feet tall.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged; drooping leaves mean it is time to water immediately.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The white spathe is not a petal but a modified leaf, and it stands for weeks before fading to green. The plant also tells you when it is thirsty: the whole thing droops, then lifts again within hours of a drink. Few houseplants ask so plainly.
